title: SOC2 control jotter — evidence mapping + questions
body:
Quick context:
I started this as a scatter of answers to the auditor's initial control questionnaire. Aim: map each control to a concrete artifact we can ship for the audit (logs, configs, policies), note gaps, and jot questions for infra/product/SRE. This is very rough — mostly notes to self and things to ask on standup.

Primary control areas I'm focusing on right now:
- Change management / code deployment (CC6-ish)
- System operations and availability (CC7)
- Logical access / least privilege (CC9)
- Vendor / third-party controls (procurement + contracts)

Observations / candidate evidence items (very raw):
- Deployments: GH actions + protected branches + required PR reviews. Evidence = PR review history (GH), branch protection policy screenshot, release notes in release-engineering repo.
- Rollouts: Console supports canary/percent rollouts. Evidence = canary config in prod manifests (k8s helm values? repo: platform/telemetry-deploys), rollout audit log entries (does console persist audit events centrally?).
- Change approvals: who signs off on infra changes? Currently a mix: infra leads approve infra PRs, product managers approve product-facing changes. Need explicit doc mapping owners -> approval types.
- Emergency changes: SRE runbook references emergency deploy process, but we need evidence that emergency changes are logged and post-mortemed. Ask SRE for the last 6 emergency deploys and associated PM notes.

Access / identity:
- Okta is our IdP. Evidence = Okta org export (user list, groups), SSO config screenshots, SAML metadata.
- Service accounts: many service-level tokens live in Vault. Evidence = rotated key logs, Vault audit logs (how long retained?).
- Principle of least privilege: need examples of role-to-policy mappings (IAM policies for cloud resources, RBAC roles in k8s). TODO: request a sample policy for "model-serving-gpu-pool" role.

Logging & monitoring:
- Audit logs: cloud audit logs (GCP/AWS) are primary. Confirm retention policy: are logs retained 13 months (auditor will ask Type II period)? If not, need to justify.
- App-level logs: runtime emits request traces + token-level latency metrics to Datadog (or internal telemetry). We can pull traces for sample user sessions as evidence. Need to create a sanitized sample trace.
- Access logs for private deployments: customers may run on-prem — evidence must show we provide guidance for local logging, but auditors may want to see our runbook for customer support access to customer environments.

Encryption & keys:
- KMS for key wrapping: we use cloud KMS + customer-managed keys for Private mode. Evidence = KMS access logs, key rotation policy doc.
- At-rest encryption: standard cloud KMS integration for storage volumes. Need a concise diagram for reviewer showing which data is encrypted and where keys live.

Control mapping (first pass):
- CC6.1 (Change control): evidence = GH PR policy, protected branch config, release notes, deployment pipeline logs (timestamped). Gap: no single consolidated change register — maybe produce an exported CSV of all prod deploys for last 12 months.
- CC7.2 (Operations & availability): evidence = SLO dashboards, incident timeline examples, postmortem folder (sre/postmortems). Gap: tie SLO error budgets to escalation policies (we have them verbally, not consistently documented).
- CC9.3 (Access reviews): evidence = quarterly access review reports from Okta/IT. Gap: need proof that reviews were actioned (screenshot + confirmation emails).

Open questions / asks to triage:
- Maya (SRE): can you export the last 12 months of deployment pipeline logs (timestamps, commit SHA, executor)? Auditor will want a continuous record. If retention < 12 months, note it.
- Jordan (Platform infra): where are Vault audit logs stored? How long retained? Need a sample of a key rotation event with timestamps.
- Product: who owns the rollout approval flow? Need a short doc describing canary thresholds and rollback criteria (console -> rollout policy).
- Legal/Procurement: do we have standard SOC2 language in our vendor contracts (for third-party hosting partners)? If not, we need to surface the top 10 vendors for vendor mgmt control.

Evidence packaging ideas (for the auditor packet):
- For each control map to: 1) policy doc, 2) configuration snapshot (screenshots or exported JSON), 3) log extract (redacted), 4) owner sign-off (email). Build a small index CSV linking these artifacts.

Risks I keep tripping over:
- Private deployments: evidence in our control environment vs customer-managed environment — auditors sometimes require us to show how we control access during support. We need a clear support access checklist + customer consent template.
- Retention mismatch: telemetry logs, Vault audits, and GH logs have different retention windows. Auditor will likely ask for continuity across the Type II period (12 months).
- Ad-hoc approvals: emergency approvals are messy — ensure each has a post-facto approval email and PM note.

Quick TODO (actionable):
- [ ] Ask SRE for deploy log export (12 months) — Maya
- [ ] Request Vault audit sample + retention policy — Jordan
- [ ] Draft a "support access to customer environments" one-pager — Samir
- [ ] Compile 3 example postmortems showing RCA and action items (last 6 months) — SRE/Product
- [ ] Export Okta group membership + past access review screenshots — IT ops
- [ ] Build the artifact index CSV template (columns: control, artifact_id, file_path, owner, date) — me (Ryan)

Notes to self on packaging: keep artifact file names predictable: audit/controls/CC6-deploys-2024-07-2025-06.json, audit/controls/CC9-access-review-2025-06.csv etc. Make sure to include redaction notes where PII or customer data would appear.

Meeting prep for next sync:
- Bring 3 example deploy records + 1 emergency deploy example
- Bring one Vault rotation event + KMS rotation policy
- Prepare a quick diagram (PPT screenshot) of where logs live and retention windows

Random thoughts / fragments:
- Could we add a nightly job that exports deployment metadata to BigQuery for easier auditor queries? Low-effort, high-value.
- If retention gaps exist, consider a "compensating control" note explaining why the missing full retention does not increase risk (e.g., quarantine snapshots, other logging sources). Need Legal sign-off on compensating control narrative.

References / links I've been glancing at:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-SEC-1123 (control catalog)
- Jira: JIRA-SOC2-98 (audit tracker)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/482 (example rollout change)

Endnote: keep this informal until we have concrete exports. Will move to shared_drives/company/misc/audit-packet once items are stable.

Last edited quick log: 2025-08-03 — added TODOs and clarified evidence packaging.
